defects.description: Batch application resolves records without rechecking the initiating actor's current ownership.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { Records } from "./src/index.js"; const r = new Records(); r.create("a","alice","draft"); r.create("b","alice","draft"); const t = r.prepareRename("alice",["a","b"],"ready"); r.transfer("alice","b","bob"); try { r.applyRename(t); } catch {} console.log(JSON.stringify([r.read("a"),r.read("b")]));'

defects.why_missed: S9(a): prepare, transfer, apply requires a changed owner between authorization and mutation. A test denying batch preparation by a stranger names authorization but never distinguishes variants; even a valid deferred batch with no intervening transfer is green on every variant.

defects.description: Undo checks historical authorship but restores a title without current-owner authorization.

trigger.input: node --input-type=module -e 'import { Records } from "./src/index.js"; const r = new Records(); r.create("a","alice","draft"); r.rename("alice","a","ready"); r.transfer("alice","a","bob"); try { r.undoRename("alice","a"); } catch {} console.log(JSON.stringify(r.read("a")));'

defects.why_missed: S9(a,d): rename, transfer, undo crosses a state-changing ownership boundary. The naive undo oracle expects the original title because the actor authored the rename; a stranger-with-no-history denial test is green in both variants.
